nodes.label: AI Letter Monogram Mark
nodes.ambiguity: Cannot verify from the asset whether 'AI' is Deepgram's own wordmark or a generic letter monogram used across the provider tile set.
nodes.description: Bold black stylized 'AI' letterform, the A and I interlocked/kerned as a single ligature, centered on a white rounded-square tile filling the full 128x128 canvas. Pure black glyph on light background, no gradients, no color accent, no enclosing frame beyond the tile's own rounded corners. Ambiguity: the mark is the two letters 'AI' only; nothing in the asset ties the letterform to a specific vendor wordmark, so whether it is a brand-accurate Deepgram mark or a generic letter monogram within the tile set cannot be determined from the image alone.

nodes.label: deepgram.png (Deepgram Provider Icon Asset)
nodes.description: Static brand/identity asset served from the frontend public dir. 128x128 PNG, 2736 bytes, 8-bit RGBA. It carries no data payload, no UI layout, no text content: it is purely a visual mark used to identify a provider entry in lists, cards, headers and topology graphs.

nodes.label: Deepgram (Speech AI Provider)
nodes.rationale: The asset filename names the vendor explicitly, and the frontend provider registry (frontend/src/shared/constants/providers.js, id 'deepgram', alias 'dg', brand color #13EF93) shows Deepgram is a real supported provider, not an asset-only stub. Note the registry carries a brand color (#13EF93) and a lucide 'mic' icon plus textIcon 'DG' fallback, while this tile is monochrome 'AI' lettering - i.e. the icon asset and the in-code brand identity are two parallel, non-derivable representations of the same vendor.

nodes.label: 128px Monochrome Provider Icon Tile Pattern
nodes.rationale: This asset belongs to a set of 106 sibling tiles in frontend/public/providers, all 128x128 (verified groq.png, assemblyai.png, azure.png match the same 128x128 canvas), each holding one high-contrast dark glyph or wordmark on a light background. Consumers render them at roughly 20px (className 'size-5 rounded object-contain') inside dense pickers, tables and status cards. The single-glyph-on-light rule is a legibility trade-off: a 20px box cannot resolve a full-color brand logo, so identity is reduced to the most distinctive letterform, and the uniform 128px canvas keeps the grid visually even when marks differ in intrinsic ink coverage.

nodes.label: Provider ID PNG Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: Every consumer in the frontend builds the asset URL by string interpolation, e.g. src={`/providers/${providerId}.png`} (Header.jsx, ModelSelectModal.jsx, media-providers pages, usage ProviderLimits cards, ProviderTopology.jsx, automation page, DefaultToolCard.jsx). Because the lookup is a raw template literal with no manifest or import map, the on-disk filename must be character-identical to the provider id, otherwise the request 404s and the onError handler sets display:none, silently rendering no icon at all. This is why an asset can exist with no import statement anywhere in the codebase yet still be load-bearing.

nodes.label: fetch-combo Provider Auto-Fallback
nodes.rationale: Model IDs end in /fetch; a combo model chains several scrape providers with automatic fallback so a failing upstream does not abort the request.

nodes.label: Provider Is The Model Invariant
nodes.rationale: "provider":"tavily" is equivalent to "model":"tavily", which removes a second dimension of configuration: the selected upstream is the selected model.

nodes.label: search-combo Provider Auto-Fallback
nodes.rationale: Models flagged owned_by:"combo" chain search providers with auto-fallback, so query availability does not depend on a single upstream engine.

nodes.label: Text-Glyph Monogram Icon Pattern (wordmark drawn as live <text>, not vector paths)

nodes.label: PayPal Donate Payment Flow (donation support)
nodes.rationale: A scannable code is embedded so viewers of the app/site can donate to the project without typing a PayPal URL or leaving the page for a checkout form; the code is the entire payment trigger.

nodes.label: 512x512 Render Surface Upscaled from 33x33 ViewBox
nodes.rationale: Authoring the symbol on a 33-unit grid keeps module boundaries on exact integers, then declaring width/height 512 gives roughly 15.5 device-independent pixels per module so the code still scans when displayed at small UI sizes or captured from a photo.

nodes.norm_label: high contrast monochrome mark (single accent hue)
nodes.rationale: Only one accent hue plus white is used, with no gradients, shadows, or outlines, so the badge stays legible at small list-item sizes and on both light and dark UI surfaces; the horizontal bar in the glyph doubles as the 'i' counter-form of the 'ALi' textIcon used elsewhere in the provider registry.

nodes.label: International Region Logo Variant (Glyph Identical To Domestic)
nodes.norm_label: international region logo variant (glyph identical to domestic)
nodes.rationale: Visually this file is pixel-equivalent in mark, tile color, and geometry to the domestic alicode.png in the same directory; the international region is signalled only by the '-intl' filename suffix, i.e. region differentiation is delegated to registry metadata (id, name, console/API-key URL) rather than to any change in the artwork.

nodes.label: Brand Identifier System (Filename As Provider Id)
nodes.norm_label: brand identifier system (filename as provider id)
nodes.rationale: The file has no embedded text; the provider identity is carried entirely by the filename 'alicode-intl', which doubles as the provider id and alias in the registry (Alibaba Intl, pointing at the international model-studio endpoint). Filename-as-id is the design decision: it lets one providers/ directory serve both the domestic and international Alibaba entries with no metadata sidecar, and lets the UI fall back to a textIcon ('ALi') when the image is missing.

nodes.label: Rounded Square Icon Tile Pattern
nodes.rationale: The mark is placed on a near-full-bleed rounded square with corner cut-outs at the glyph's three junctions, so the glyph reads as a cut-out of the tile rather than a logo floating on transparent background. This keeps the asset visually consistent with the other provider icons in the providers/ directory, which all use the same tile shape so the provider list renders as a uniform grid of equal-weight square badges.

nodes.label: K + Blue Dot Reads as Stylized 'Ki' Monogram
nodes.norm_label: k + blue dot reads as stylized 'ki' monogram
nodes.rationale: Design intent: the white 'K' alone is an incomplete initial, so the brand adds a small blue dot in the upper-right quadrant, positioned where a lowercase 'i' tittle would sit. The dot is the only saturated color in the asset, which both completes the 'Ki' ligature reading and encodes the vendor's blue as the single accent hue. Consequence: the mark stays legible at 16-24px provider-selector sizes because the identifying detail is a single high-contrast point rather than a second letterform.

nodes.label: Kimi Rounded-Square Icon Tile
nodes.rationale: The asset is a 128x128 RGBA PNG whose visible art is a dark near-black rounded square with softened corners rather than a full-bleed rectangle. This is the shared tile shape used across the frontend/public/providers icon set, so every provider badge occupies the same footprint and optical weight in lists, dropdowns, and chat headers; a single source file must therefore satisfy uniform scaling, dark-mode contrast, and small-size legibility at once.

nodes.rationale: Placed in frontend/public/providers alongside 105 sibling provider logos, this file exists to be resolved as a static image asset when the UI renders a provider entry; the naming convention (kebab-case provider slug + .png) is the contract that lets the provider list component reference it without a build-time registry entry.

nodes.label: Bar Chart / Equalizer Bar Motif
nodes.rationale: Unequal-height vertical bars are the classic visual shorthand for a histogram or audio equalizer, so the mark signals generative throughput and media pipelines without a single rendered example image — a deliberate choice for a provider whose outputs are pictures and video.

nodes.label: Weavy Bar-Glyph Brandmark
nodes.rationale: Brandmark is built from five axis-aligned solid rectangles on a white field: three tall bars in an upper row plus two shorter bars suspended below and between them. Pure geometry, no curves, no gradients, so the mark renders identically across light and dark surfaces and survives downscaling to list-row or favicon size where fine detail would disappear.

nodes.label: Flat Monochrome High-Contrast Logo Treatment
nodes.rationale: Single-colour, hard-edge treatment with no text lockup and a 200x200 square raster crop: one file can back the provider picker row, the proxy allowlist entry and any badge without a separate monochrome variant or a text lockup asset.

nodes.rationale: The providers/ directory holds 105 sibling raster/SVG assets, one per supported LLM and voice provider, named by provider slug. One-file-per-provider with slug filenames keeps icon lookup a static, bundler-friendly import instead of a runtime resolve, and keeps the provider catalogue legible as a directory listing. nodes.rationale: Startup guidance is inserted before broader repo exploration so bucket selection happens first, and memory is appended back after meaningful work.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure Read Strategy
nodes.rationale: Read only session.md when the task is unrelated, one or two buckets when it matches, and context files only when a bucket points to needed detail, so recall never inflates the main context window.

nodes.label: Non-Destructive Root Instruction File Merge
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md are updated by insertion or merge, never replaced: repo-specific rules are preserved and only Multi Brain startup guidance is appended.

nodes.label: Two-Level Shared Memory Index
nodes.rationale: Shared memory across agents is enabled without forcing every agent to read every detail: a small master index plus task-oriented buckets plus pointed deep context files.

nodes.label: Mandatory Skill Invocation Rule
nodes.rationale: A 1% chance a skill applies forces invocation before any response or action, because the check is cheap and the model cannot rationalize its way past a listed red flag.

nodes.label: AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE Behind TLS Proxy
nodes.rationale: Keep AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=false when the proxy terminates TLS and talks plain HTTP to the container; the app cannot know the client-facing scheme.

nodes.label: Mandatory /data Volume Mount
nodes.rationale: SQLite is a file; without a volume at /data every container recreate destroys the database, which is the documented 'data gone after recreate' symptom.

nodes.label: better-sqlite3 musl Prebuild Requirement
nodes.rationale: Custom builds fail on better-sqlite3 install because Node 22 alpine needs musl prebuilds, so package-lock.json must not be stripped.

nodes.label: No Automatic SQLite/PostgreSQL Store Sync
nodes.rationale: Switching DATABASE_URL requires an explicit dashboard export then import; the stores never sync themselves, so a switch without export silently presents an empty database.

nodes.label: SSE Proxy Buffering Disabled
nodes.rationale: proxy_buffering off plus a 300s read timeout is mandatory because streaming chat completions would otherwise be buffered by the proxy and appear frozen to the client.

nodes.label: postgres Compose Profile Gate
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL sits behind a `postgres` profile so the default SQLite path starts with one service; enabling it requires explicitly setting DATABASE_URL to point at it.

nodes.label: DATA_DIR Environment Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Plain `npm run dev` has no dotenv loader so it falls back to ~/.9router-v3 while start.sh and Docker export backend/.env; the documented 'data is gone' symptom is this split, not data loss.

nodes.label: Error Sanitizer Redaction
nodes.rationale: Logs must never print API keys or tokens, so the error sanitizer redacts sk-…, Bearer …, and key/token fields; docker log grepping is the documented way to verify no secret leaked.

nodes.label: Fail-Fast On PostgreSQL Unreachable
nodes.rationale: The server refuses to start when DATABASE_URL is set but PostgreSQL is unreachable instead of silently falling back to SQLite; a silent fallback would put data in the wrong store with no signal.

nodes.label: font-display: swap Policy
nodes.rationale: `block` was deliberately rejected: it holds icons invisible for 3s then paints the ligature name at full text size, which is how icon names previously rendered as oversized words.

nodes.label: getAdapter() DB Access Boundary
nodes.rationale: All database access must go through backend/src/lib/db getAdapter(); opening SQLite directly would bypass the dialect abstraction that lets the same code run on PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Shared Working-Model Eligibility Rule
nodes.rationale: The working definition is duplicated in backend and frontend and must be kept in sync; a divergence would make the Models-page Working filter disagree with GET /api/models/working.

nodes.label: DashboardLayout Suspense Boundary Scope
nodes.rationale: The boundary wraps only <Outlet>. Wrapping the whole router lets a lazy chunk load unmount the sidebar and header and flash a full-screen fallback.
